title: Generative language models exhibit social identity biases

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting language models to complete sentences starting with 'We are...' (ingroup) and 'They are...' (outgroup), and applying sentiment analysis classifiers (RoBERTa and VADER) to calculate the odds ratios for ingroup solidarity (positive sentiment) and outgroup hostility (negative sentiment).

Fine-tuning models on partisan Twitter corpora (US Republicans and Democrats) to measure the amplification of ingroup/outgroup sentiment disparities, and evaluating specific political identity prompts (e.g., 'As US Republicans, we are...').

Prompting language models with specific gender identities (e.g., 'As women, we are...', 'As men, they are...') to evaluate whether the fundamental ingroup solidarity and outgroup hostility sentiment effects manifest for these specific demographic groups.
